heading: Building a robot for the US market? Start here.
paragraphs: The Federal Communications Commission, or FCC, regulates radio and digital equipment entering the US market. Most connected robots need equipment authorization before import or sale. The Covered List can block that route for equipment considered a national security risk.

Before choosing suppliers, check two things: whether the finished robot falls within a restricted equipment category, and whether its electronics come from a producer covered by the component rules. Start with the robot, then use the reference below to look up suppliers and collect the records your reviewer needs.

heading: Already selling a robot? Check the existing authorization
paragraphs: An existing FCC authorization can let a company keep selling an established model after a new restriction takes effect. What matters is the authorization covering that model and configuration. A first sale, preorder or product announcement does not establish that protection.

The FCC’s July robotics guidance allows continued imports, marketing and sales of existing models that already received equipment authorization. The separate component rule effective October 13, 2026 also preserves previously authorized equipment under its existing authorization. This is often called being “grandfathered,” but it does not give the company permission to launch any future model.

callouts.title: Keep selling the authorized model
callouts.body: The protection concerns the existing model, not just units already sitting in a warehouse. Confirm that additional units match the authorized configuration and remain within its authorization.

callouts.title: Support robots customers already own
callouts.body: The robotics guidance permits continued use of already authorized devices, repairs and replacement with identical parts. A replacement that changes the design needs a separate assessment.

callouts.title: Check an application already in progress
callouts.body: An application filed before October 13, 2026 and still pending on that date is exempt from the new component prohibition. If it is later amended to add, substitute or change the relevant electronic hardware, that amendment is treated as a new application. A pending application is not permission to sell.

callouts.title: Review a new version before shipping it
callouts.body: An earlier approval does not automatically cover a new model, different electronics or a changed producer or manufacturing arrangement. Have the lab or certification body determine whether the change remains within the existing authorization, needs a permitted modification or requires a new authorization. A change that makes equipment covered cannot rely on the old approval.

heading: How a telecom security policy reached robotics
paragraphs: The FCC’s Covered List grew out of US efforts to protect communications networks from equipment considered a national security risk. Congress created the list through the Secure Networks Act and later directed the FCC to stop approving covered equipment for the US market.

The concern now extends to connected machines. In its robotics determination, the government cited the potential for remote interference, access to sensitive sensor data and dependence on foreign supply chains. The component rule addresses a related concern: changing the brand on a finished product does not remove the risks attributed to electronics inside it.

heading: 1. Check the complete robot
paragraphs: Start with the machine you plan to sell. The July 2026 entry for foreign produced advanced robotic devices can apply even when none of your component suppliers is named on the list. A connected floor cleaner, delivery robot or mobile inspection platform should be checked against the full definition.

The definition combines the following characteristics. It also contains exclusions, including fixed stationary industrial and medical arms, specified connected vehicles, rail only vehicles, aircraft, underwater vehicles and classified medical devices.

heading: 2. Check the electronics inside it
paragraphs: Since October 13, 2026, FCC 26-50 also restricts new authorizations for devices containing certain electronic hardware from a named Covered List producer. Two conditions must hold: the component comes from a producer covered by a company based entry, and that entry would bar the finished device if the same producer had made it.

Read the equipment description and intended use together. For example, the Hikvision, Dahua and Hytera entries specify security uses. A camera’s function in your product matters to that assessment. A production location entry alone does not make every component from that producer subject to this separate rule.

The rule calls the relevant electronics “logic bearing hardware.” Begin with assemblies that process, store or transfer digital information, including the controls inside a smart battery pack. Ask suppliers for the records below.

heading: Look up a producer or equipment category
paragraphs: Search the actual producer, which may differ from the distributor or brand on the box. Open an entry to see its scope, then check the official record for current wording and exceptions. A name match needs a product review; an absent name does not resolve a production category or affiliate question.

heading: 3. Get the supplier records
paragraphs: A bill of materials, or BOM, is your product’s parts list. Record exact models and revisions, the actual producers, manufacturing locations and the evidence supplied. For purchased boards, request information about the installed chips and modules needed to resolve the review.
Use the request below with suppliers while you are still comparing parts. Keep their replies with your design revision, and ask to be notified before they substitute a part or change its production.

heading: 4. Take the open question to the right expert
paragraphs: Bring a short product description, intended use, planned manufacturing location, current parts list and supplier replies. Identify the decision you need: the approval route, an uncertain producer or a restriction that may apply to your configuration.

heading: Before you prepare for sale
paragraphs: Agree the authorization route with your lab early. Keep the resulting records tied to the configuration you will ship, including its radio modules and approved substitutes.
